quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed the same to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Put the car in neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, or deep puddles. These surfaces can cause your car to skid. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your driving lane?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals for you to return.
When you signal for three seconds.
When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you have enough space from the car you passed. Check your rearview mirror. When you see both headlights of the passed vehicle, you have enough room to return to your lane.

questions.question: What shape and color are construction zone signs?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. You will find these signs on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash.
Higher speeds mean you need a longer following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is almost impossible. Faster driving also increases stopping distance, so increase your following distance when you drive faster.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times quickly.
Slow down gradually without using the brake.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brake.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Remove your foot from the accelerator. Do not brake. Let the car slow on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming vehicle has bright headlights on and you cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane. Watch the other vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
The road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards just ahead. This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: You and the driver on your left reach a four-way stop sign at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You.
Whoever signals to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time to a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What may happen?

options.text: The truck may use either of the two lanes.
The truck may have to swing wide to complete the turn.
The truck must stay in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck may have to swing wide to complete the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need more space to turn right. They often swing wide to complete the turn safely.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your driving?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: A yellow traffic light warns that it will change to red soon. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Keep going and safely clear the intersection.
Speed up to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going and safely clear the intersection.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, drive through as quickly as you can to clear it safely.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause longer stopping distances and worse crashes. As you drive faster, a crash becomes more severe and serious injuries are more likely. Leave more space between your vehicle and others when driving at higher speeds.

questions.question: You should use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days so that:

options.text: Your engine stays warm.
Other drivers can see your vehicle.
You can warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: When it rains, snows, or gets foggy, other drivers have trouble seeing your vehicle. Headlights make your vehicle more visible. If you need to use your windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is turning left, what can they do?

options.text: Use the left lane.
Cut across all lanes.
Wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic in the road, just like cars. When turning left, they may use the left lane like any other vehicle.

questions.question: When must drivers use their headlights?

options.text: From half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise
During the day in clear weather
When they feel tired

questions.correctAnswerText: From half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise
questions.explanation: You must use headlights from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise. Use them anytime you cannot see 200 feet ahead.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams bounce off moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your car.
Avoid driving next to it for long periods.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving next to it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have big blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside them for long periods where the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than other vehicles.
Drive at that same speed.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at that same speed.
questions.explanation: Match your speed to the traffic around you (as long as it is within the speed limit). Vehicles traveling at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when some vehicles travel at different speeds than others.

questions.question: Your license can be suspended if you are under 21 and have a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot have any alcohol in their system. If police find any trace of alcohol, you will lose your license for two years and face other penalties.

questions.question: You are in a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can do so safely.
Never move your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: After a collision where no one is hurt, move your vehicle out of traffic if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You are stopped at a red traffic light with a green arrow. When can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane. The intersection must be clear. You must always let pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection pass safely.

questions.question: Why is it more dangerous to drive at night than during the day?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery.
Your reaction time is slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far down the road as you can during the day. Headlights from other cars can also cause glare. Always use your headlights and drive carefully when it is dark.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down your body and mind. It reduces your ability to focus and stay alert. It also lowers your judgment.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly blocks traffic.
Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly blocks traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, do not drive so slowly that you block other vehicles. Driving too slowly can result in a ticket.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Stop sign ahead.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is slippery when it is wet. Wet roads are dangerous and you can lose control of your car. Slow down when you see wet pavement because it takes longer to stop.
